items.title: Haiti: Signs of hope despite gang violence and political uncertainty
items.summary: For millions of Haitians, daily life has become a struggle to stay safe, find enough food and simply move around their own neighbourhood.

items.title: Ukraine: UN condemns overnight attack on Kyiv
items.summary: United Nations agencies have deplored a fresh Russian assault on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv which left at least one person dead and a dozen injured.

items.title: A former Ferrari boss has a blunt message: Your commute is more dangerous than his old job
items.summary: Jean Todt spent decades around the deadliest motorsport on Earth. He was a rally co‑driver, then ran Ferrari’s Formula One team, then became president of world motorsport’s governing body. In his early years, a driver dying at the track barely made news.

items.title: Baristas behind bars: Thai prisoners brew a path back to daily life
items.summary: It looks like a regular coffee shop, albeit set up in an old red bus. Stairs lead up to a serving hatch, with a menu of drink options. A selection of jaunty coffee-related messages like “My one and only love: Americano” and “Miss you a latte,” adorn the side of the bus.

items.title: Djibouti: Emergency alert spotlights sharp hunger spike
items.summary: More than 256,000 people in Djibouti – around 25 per cent of the population – are likely to face crisis or emergency level hunger over the coming months, a UN-backed global food monitoring network warned in a new report released Friday.

items.title: Guterres: AI must be shaped by 'all of humanity', not a handful of powers
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Friday urged governments and technology companies to work together to ensure artificial intelligence (AI) benefits all countries.

items.title: Hunger deepens for displaced families in Sudan’s El Obeid
items.summary: UN humanitarians working in war-torn Sudan on Friday highlighted rapidly growing needs among the more than 100,000 displaced people now sheltering in camps in the city of El Obeid.

items.title: US-Iran war: UN chief calls for new diplomatic push following attacks on civilian areas
items.summary: The UN Secretary-General remains deeply concerned by the continuing deadly military escalation between Iran and the United States, his spokesperson said on Friday as attacks destroyed key civilian and military infrastructure across the Gulf region.

items.title: World News in Brief: Appeal for calm in Kashmir, women on the move, Ebola deaths mount, 12th anniversary of MH17
items.summary: The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, has appealed for calm in Pakistan-Administered Kashmir amid unrest ahead of regional elections.

items.title: ‘Heat deaths are not inevitable’: WHO pushes Europe to heat‑proof its hospitals
items.summary: As Europe battles a deadly record-breaking heatwave, the World Health Organization (WHO) issued new guidance on Thursday to help countries face scorching temperatures now and in the future.

items.title: As aid dries up, countries pledge to close the $4 trillion development gap
items.summary: UN Member States reaffirmed their commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by adopting a declaration on Wednesday that they will implement reforms to help close the $4 trillion SDG financing gap.

items.title: Breaking the silence: Zimbabwean youth leader calls for urgent investment in mental health
items.summary: For Tanatswa Amanda Chikaura, mental health advocacy began with a personal loss: while studying psychology at the University of Zimbabwe, she learned that a fellow student had died by suicide.

items.title: Gaza farmers battle to rebuild as WFP warns of West Bank settler violence
items.summary: The UN is supporting farmers in Gaza who are struggling to rebuild their smallholdings in areas devastated by the Hamas-Israel war.

items.title: Haiti: Training the next generation to fight corruption
items.summary: How do you tackle corruption in a country grappling with insecurity, weak institutions and widespread impunity? In Haiti, the Government and the United Nations are betting on the country's youth.
